newsitem.title: THAILAND: Solarz applauds Hun Sen willingness for mediation.
newsitem.headline: Solarz applauds Hun Sen willingness for mediation.

text.p: The U.S. special envoy on Cambodia on Thursday applauded strongman Hun Sen's decision to allow the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) to play a role in trying to resolve the Cambodian crisis.

"We are encouraged by what now appears to be a willingness on the part of Hun Sen to accept the ASEAN offer to use its good offices to facilitate a political resolution of the Cambodian crisis," Solarz told reporters after meeting Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.

Solarz, who is on a whirlwind diplomatic tour of Asian capitals seeking a solution to the turmoil in Cambodia, said the United States hoped to work closely with ASEAN to try and find a solution to the problem.

Cambodia was to have joined ASEAN on Wednesday, but Hun Sen's bloody overthrow of First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh earlier this month led the regional organisation to postpone Cambodia's admission to the group indefinitely.

Hun Sen had originally rejected ASEAN's efforts to mediate and help find a political solution to the crisis. He told a group of ASEAN foreign ministers in Phnom Penh on Saturday that he did not want their intervention.

But Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot, who has been named by Hun Sen to replace Ranariddh, told ASEAN ministers in Malaysia on Wednesday Hun Sen had changed his mind and was willing to accept mediation.

Solarz said Thailand, like the United States, hoped to find a solution to the Cambodia problem that is compatible with the 1991 Paris Peace Accords, which paved the way for United Nations-sponsored elections in 1993.

"We both (Chavalit and Solarz) hope that this problem can be resolved in a way that is compatible with the Paris Agreement and which will make possible genuine national reconciliation in Cambodia and a truly and genuinely free and fair election next year,' said Solarz, a former U.S. congressman who was involved in talks leading to the Paris Peace Agreement.

Cambodia was due to hold an election next year. Hun Sen has said the poll will still take place but Ranariddh said on Saturday under the current circumstances -- with many opposition politicians out of the country -- it would not be a fair poll.

Dozens of politicians loyal to Ranariddh and his FUNCINPEC party fled the country in the wake of the fighting as they said they feared for their lives. Diplomats in Phnom Penh have said there were at least 40 politically motivated killings after Ranariddh's ouster.
Solarz said he hoped all opposition politicians would be able to return to Cambodia to participate in the election.
Ranariddh, who left Cambodia on the eve of the July 5-6 fighting in Phnom Penh, was due to meet Solarz later on Thursday before the envoy headed to Phnom Penh to meet Hun Sen.

"I do not underestimate the difficulties in achieving a satisfactory solution. But I am hopeful if the United States and other countries...can work closely with ASEAN...to resolve this matter, that we may ultimately be able to succeed," said Solarz.
